chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave woman whom her husband had not yet consummated the marriage with, who died and left behind her mother, two full siblings (from father and mother), a paternal grandfather (father of the mother), and her husband. He said: 'The husband is given half, and the mother is given the remainder, and the grandfather is given nothing because his daughter (the mother of the deceased) has blocked him from the inheritance, and the siblings are given nothing.'
ai.seo_question: How is the estate distributed for a slave woman who dies with a non-consummating husband, mother, grandfather, and siblings?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific case of a slave woman (*umm walad* or simply *mamlukah*) whose husband had not consummated the marriage, establishing that he receives half the estate while the mother takes the remainder as a residual heir. The grandfather and siblings are excluded (*hujb*) because the mother, as a closer ascendant, blocks the grandfather, and the presence of the mother blocks the siblings from receiving a share in this configuration. This ruling highlights the Shia principle of *hujb* (blocking) where closer relatives exclude more distant ones, distinct from the Sunni view where the grandfather might share with the mother.
